# wow64gen deep-marshal list — Nt* syscalls whose `ptr` args point at a struct
# whose 32-bit and 64-bit layouts DIFFER, so ABI-level arg widening is not
# enough. wow64gen emits these as WOW64_NEEDS_MANUAL stubs; implement each by
# hand in wow64_manual.c (translate the 32-bit struct into a 64-bit one on the
# stack, call the real Nt*, copy any output back). One name per line; # starts
# a comment. Re-run wow64gen after editing.
#
# Seeded with the highest-frequency structural offenders. This is intentionally
# INCOMPLETE — add names as boot coverage exercises more of the surface. When
# unsure whether a syscall belongs here, list it: a loud manual stub is always
# safer than a silently-wrong auto thunk.
#
# Categories:
# --- OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES takers (ObjectName is a 32-bit UNICODE_STRING* whose
#     Buffer is a 32-bit ptr; the 64-bit struct is wider) ---
# --- IO_STATUS_BLOCK.Information is ULONG_PTR (4 vs 8 bytes) + these carry
#     OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES and/or overlapped state ---
# --- context / LARGE_INTEGER-by-value / arrays of pointers ---
NtAllocateVirtualMemory
NtCreateDirectoryObject
NtCreateEvent
NtCreateFile
NtCreateKey
NtCreateMailslotFile
NtCreateMutant
NtCreateNamedPipeFile
NtCreateSection
NtCreateSemaphore
NtCreateSymbolicLinkObject
NtDeviceIoControlFile
NtFreeVirtualMemory
NtFsControlFile
NtMapViewOfSection
NtNotifyChangeDirectoryFile
NtOpenDirectoryObject
NtOpenEvent
NtOpenFile
NtOpenKey
NtQueryValueKey
NtOpenMutant
NtOpenProcess
NtOpenSection
NtOpenSemaphore
NtOpenSymbolicLinkObject
NtOpenThread
NtProtectVirtualMemory
NtQueryAttributesFile
NtQueryDirectoryFile
NtQueryFullAttributesFile
NtQueryInformationProcess
NtQueryInformationThread
NtQueryObject
NtQuerySymbolicLinkObject
NtQuerySystemInformation
NtQueryVirtualMemory
NtSetSystemInformation
NtQuerySection
NtCreateKeyedEvent
NtOpenKeyedEvent
NtConnectPort
NtSecureConnectPort
# M19: PORT_MESSAGE is 24 bytes to a 32-bit guest and 40 to the host, so the
# flat thunk handed the kernel a header whose TotalLength was 16 short of what
# `DataLength + sizeof(PORT_MESSAGE) > TotalLength` demands -- every call
# returned c000000d before it reached a port.
NtRequestWaitReplyPort
NtContinue
# E5: EXCEPTION_RECORD32 + CONTEXT32 — the flat thunk fed both to the 64-bit
# kernel at 64-bit layout. Dispatched directly into the guest's own SEH.
NtRaiseException
# M8: kernel->user callback completion — the guest's 32-bit result buffer
# must be translated per in-flight callback type (wow64_callback.c).
NtCallbackReturn
# --- M10: the IO_STATUS_BLOCK family ---
# Every one of these takes an IO_STATUS_BLOCK, whose `ULONG_PTR Information` is
# 4 bytes on i386 and 8 on the host: the guest's struct is 8 bytes, the host
# kernel writes 16. Auto-thunking them (which is what happened before M10) both
# overflows the guest struct by 8 bytes AND reads Information from the wrong
# offset. The first six + NtQueryDirectoryFile are implemented in wow64_manual.c
# (Doom needs ReadFile); the rest are listed so they fail LOUD instead of
# silently corrupting the guest — implement on demand.
NtReadFile
NtWriteFile
NtQueryInformationFile
NtSetInformationFile
NtQueryVolumeInformationFile
NtFlushBuffersFile
NtSetVolumeInformationFile
NtReadFileScatter
NtWriteFileGather
NtLockFile
NtUnlockFile
NtQueryEaFile
NtSetEaFile
NtQueryQuotaInformationFile
NtSetQuotaInformationFile
NtCancelIoFile
NtCancelIoFileEx
NtCancelSynchronousIoFile
NtNotifyChangeKey
NtNotifyChangeMultipleKeys
NtRemoveIoCompletion
NtRemoveIoCompletionEx
NtCreateIoCompletion
NtOpenIoCompletion
NtCreateThread
NtGetContextThread
NtSetContextThread
NtOpenProcessTokenEx
NtOpenThreadTokenEx
NtWaitForMultipleObjects
NtTerminateThread

# --- E17: the CPU layer's memory-notification contract. A JIT host only
#     decodes guest addresses it has been told are executable and caches
#     translations keyed on guest address, so every change to the 32-bit
#     address space has to be announced. These are ABI-flat (except the
#     ULONG_PTR *ReturnSize on the Read/Write pair, which the flat thunk
#     overwrote 8 bytes of) — they are here for the side effect. ---
NtUnmapViewOfSection
NtReadVirtualMemory
NtWriteVirtualMemory
NtFlushInstructionCache
NtSetInformationProcess

# --- E19: the out-cell class. Each of these takes a guest pointer to a cell
#     the kernel fills with a POINTER-SIZED value (HANDLE, base address,
#     region size). Flat-thunked, the kernel's 8-byte store ran four bytes
#     past the 4-byte cell the guest declared — a successful call that
#     silently corrupts whatever the guest put next to the variable.
#     Sourced from `marshalgen audit`, not from memory: note that
#     NtOpenProcessTokenEx/NtOpenThreadTokenEx above were already marshalled
#     while the plain variants right here were not. ---
NtOpenProcessToken
NtOpenThreadToken
NtDuplicateObject
NtGetNextProcess
NtGetNextThread
NtDuplicateToken
NtCreateEventPair
NtOpenEventPair
NtCreateJobObject
NtOpenJobObject
NtOpenTimer
NtCreateTimer
NtCreateDebugObject
NtCreatePort
NtCreateWaitablePort
NtCreateProcess
NtCreateProcessEx
NtCreateProfile
NtLockVirtualMemory
NtUnlockVirtualMemory
NtFlushVirtualMemory

# --- E20: bare PUNICODE_STRING / POBJECT_ATTRIBUTES arguments. UNICODE_STRING
#     is 8 bytes in the guest and 16 on the host, so Buffer sits at offset 4
#     there and offset 8 here: a flat thunk made the kernel read the string
#     POINTER FROM PAST THE END of the guest's struct. Not a truncation -- a
#     wholly unrelated address, while Length/MaximumLength (same offsets) came
#     through intact and made it look plausible.
#     NtSetValueKey is the one that mattered: it BUGCHECKed the box (0x1E,
#     ProbeForRead on the garbage pointer), so every RegSetValueEx from a
#     32-bit guest was a local DoS. NtQueryValueKey was ALREADY marshalled --
#     reads worked, writes killed the machine. ---
NtSetValueKey
NtDeleteValueKey
NtRenameKey
NtDeleteFile
NtDisplayString
NtLoadDriver
NtUnloadDriver
NtQuerySystemEnvironmentValue
NtSetSystemEnvironmentValue
NtQuerySystemEnvironmentValueEx
NtSetSystemEnvironmentValueEx
NtCreatePagingFile
NtLoadKey
NtLoadKey2
NtLoadKeyEx
NtReplaceKey
NtUnloadKey
NtUnloadKey2
NtUnloadKeyEx
NtQueryOpenSubKeys

NtCloseObjectAuditAlarm
NtDeleteObjectAuditAlarm
NtPrivilegeObjectAuditAlarm

# User APCs: the routine is 32-bit code, which the native KiUserApcDispatcher
# would call as native. Queued as wow64's Wow64ApcRoutine with the guest's
# routine and context packed into the 64-bit context (wow64_callback.c).
NtQueueApcThread

# wow64gen deep-marshal list for the WIN32K table (NtGdi*/NtUser*, ordered by
# win32ss/w32ksvc32.h; guest EAX carries 0x1000+index). Same rules as
# manual.txt: one name per line, # comments; a listed name becomes a loud
# WOW64_NEEDS_MANUAL stub routed to Wow64ManualDispatch (wow64_manual.c).
#
# GDI/USER structs are mostly pointer-free and identical 32/64 (RECT, POINT,
# SIZE, COLORREF, LOGBRUSH sans hooks...), so auto zero-extension covers far
# more of this table than the ntdll one. List here the calls whose args embed
# POINTERS or ULONG_PTR fields (UNICODE_STRING, DEVMODEW+driver extra,
# LOGFONT arrays with pointers, MSG with ULONG_PTR wParam...).
#
# Bring-up policy: intentionally MINIMAL — every unlisted call with a
# divergent struct will misbehave loudly under the per-syscall trace; add it
# here + a marshaller when boot coverage hits it.

# gui32.exe bring-up path (CreateDCA -> NtGdiOpenDCW: UNICODE_STRING device
# name + optional DEVMODEW + PVOID* output slot)
NtGdiOpenDCW

# MSG out-param (ULONG_PTR wParam / LPARAM widen) — the user32 pump family,
# listed pre-emptively so a future window pump never runs a silently-wrong
# auto thunk.
NtUserGetMessage
NtUserPeekMessage
NtUserDispatchMessage

# user32 per-process win32k handshake: USERCONNECT is layout-divergent
# (SHAREDINFO pointers widen; 0x124 -> 0x240). Task #29.
NtUserProcessConnect

# M8 window-creation path: pointer-bearing structs (WNDCLASSEX/CLSMENUNAME,
# LARGE_STRING, PAINTSTRUCT) + the message pump family above.
NtUserRegisterClassExWOW
# E4b: GetClassInfoExW/A — UNICODE_STRING32 name IN + 48-byte WNDCLASSEXW32 OUT
# (the auto-thunk's 80-byte kernel write corrupted 32 bytes of guest stack, and
# its garbage UNICODE_STRING Buffer bugchecked amd64 0x1E)
NtUserGetClassInfo
# E4c: winmine's menu bar — MENUITEMINFOW 48->80 + caption UNICODE_STRING
# (auto-thunk's 8-byte US32 hit an align-8 ProbeForRead -> 0x80000002 -> 0x1E)
NtUserThunkedMenuItemInfo
# E6: calc's class-atom lookup — NtUserGetAtomName(ATOM, PUNICODE_STRING). The
# win32u.spec (long ptr) flat thunk fed win32k a US32 as US64 (garbage Buffer,
# kernel writes atom name through it) -> 0x1E. In/out US32<->US64 marshal.
NtUserGetAtomName
# E6: calc's class-name query — NtUserGetClassName(HWND, BOOL, PUNICODE_STRING).
# Same US32<->US64 gap; 4-aligned US32 vs align-8 ProbeForWrite -> 0x80000002.
NtUserGetClassName
# E6: the single-PUNICODE_STRING NtUser* class, all flat-typed in win32u.spec
# (same US32<->US64 gap any GUI app hits). RegisterWindowMessage (IN),
# GetKeyboardLayoutName (in/out).
NtUserRegisterWindowMessage
NtUserGetKeyboardLayoutName
# E8: regedit/comctl32 class teardown. NtUserUnregisterClass(PUNICODE_STRING
# ClassNameOrAtom, HINSTANCE, PCLSMENUNAME) is typed flat (ptr ptr ptr), so the
# auto-thunk fed 64-bit win32k the guest's 8-byte US32 as a 16-byte US64 ->
# garbage Buffer -> ProbeAndCaptureUnicodeStringOrAtom raw_move C0000005 ->
# BUGCHECK 0x1E. Widen arg0 US32<->US64 (atom form survives); pClassMenuName is
# ignored kernel-side. Same class as GetClassName/GetAtomName above.
NtUserUnregisterClass
# E9: the flat-typed PUNICODE_STRING NtUser* sweep. A spec-vs-prototype scan
# found the whole class typed flat (ptr) in win32u.spec while the real prototype
# takes 1-2 PUNICODE_STRINGs -> the auto-thunk US32-as-US64 garbage-Buffer ->
# raw_move C0000005 -> BUGCHECK 0x1E (osk.exe hit NtUserFindWindowEx). Each is a
# pure US32<->US64 widen (Wow64pUS32to64) with non-US args flat; see wow64_manual.c.
NtUserFindWindowEx
NtUserGetWOWClass
NtUserSetWindowsHookEx
NtUserSetWinEventHook
NtUserRegisterUserApiHook
NtUserDrawCaptionTemp
NtUserLoadKeyboardLayoutEx
NtUserEnumDisplaySettings
NtUserEnumDisplayDevices
# CreateDesktop ALSO carries a divergent struct (OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES). A guest
# reached it (user32:winstation); marshaller in wow64_manual.c beside its
# Open/CreateWindowStation siblings.
NtUserCreateDesktop
# GetIconInfo: ICONINFO's HBITMAPs widen and both strings are IN/OUT. Guest
# GetIconInfo/CopyImage reached it (user32:class); marshaller in wow64_manual.c.
NtUserGetIconInfo
# ExtGetObjectW: the kernel answers in 64-bit BITMAP/DIBSECTION/LOGBRUSH/
# EXTLOGPEN layouts (each has a pointer-width field), and refuses a BITMAP
# buffer smaller than its own. Guest GetObject on any bitmap returned 0.
NtGdiExtGetObjectW
# E10: found MECHANICALLY by `marshalgen audit` (vibeos-cli check) instead of by
# the next applet to bugcheck — it diffs every LIVE flat thunk in the generated
# table against its real header prototype using clang's 32/64 record layouts.
# These have marshallers in wow64_manual.c:
#   NtGdiCreateDIBSection    PVOID *ppvBits -> the E7 overrun on a HOT path
#                            (guest gdi32 passes a 4-byte &bmBits; the kernel
#                            stored 8 bytes there on every DIB section).
#   NtUserResolveDesktop     PUNICODE_STRING path + HWINSTA* OUT (both halves).
#   NtUserOpenDesktop        \  OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES 24->48 with a nested
#   NtUserOpenWindowStation   > UNICODE_STRING — reuses Wow64pMarshalOa, the
#   NtUserCreateWindowStation/  helper the whole ntdll open family runs on.
NtGdiCreateDIBSection
#   NtUserTranslateAccelerator \  the rest of the MSG family (28 -> 48 bytes).
#   NtUserCallMsgFilter         > The pump three were marshalled in M8; these
#   NtUserRealInternalGetMessage/ three siblings were left flat and are all on
#                                 ordinary app paths (accelerator tables, modal
#                                 loops/MSGF_* hooks, user32's internal pump).
NtUserTranslateAccelerator
NtUserCallMsgFilter
NtUserRealInternalGetMessage
NtUserResolveDesktop
NtUserOpenDesktop
NtUserOpenWindowStation
NtUserCreateWindowStation
# E10, no dispatch entry: each carries a divergent struct no ladder guest
# reaches, so per the M18 rule ("never ship a marshaller no guest can disprove")
# they get the loud WOW64_AUTOMARSHAL_UNIMPL stub — a clean error instead of the
# silent-wrong flat thunk they had. A marshaller lands when a guest arrives.
#   NtUserSetCursorContents  ICONINFO (HBITMAP fields widen; 20 -> 32 bytes)
#   NtGdiAddEmbFontToDC      PVOID *pFontID OUT slot
#   NtGdiFONTOBJ_cGetGlyphs  PVOID *ppvGlyph OUT slot (a driver DDI, not an app path)
#   NtGdiDd*/NtGdiDvp*/NtGdiDxg*  DirectDraw/D3D HANDLE* + SIZE_T* OUT slots
NtUserSetCursorContents
NtGdiAddEmbFontToDC
NtGdiFONTOBJ_cGetGlyphs
NtGdiDdCreateD3DBuffer
NtGdiDdCreateSurface
NtGdiDvpAcquireNotification
NtGdiDvpUpdateVideoPort
NtGdiDxgGenericThunk
# E7: Enum{,Child,Thread}Windows -> NtUserBuildHwndList fills a caller HWND[] and
# returns the count. The flat (ptr) auto-thunk let 64-bit win32k write 8-byte
# HWNDs into the guest's sizeof(HWND)=4-byte-per-entry buffer -> 2x heap OVERRUN
# that clobbered the adjacent block (calc's button-enum corrupted the guest heap;
# surfaced as a NULL free-list Blink in RtlpRemoveFreeBlock minutes later). The
# marshaller fills a host 64-bit scratch array, then narrows each handle back.
NtUserBuildHwndList
NtUserCreateWindowEx
NtUserTranslateMessage
NtUserBeginPaint
NtUserEndPaint

# M9 default-cursor load (LoadCursor(NULL, IDC_ARROW) during first window's
# class setup): module/resource UNICODE_STRINGs widen 8->16 (align-8 probe),
# and SetCursorIconData's CURSORDATA has pointer/HBITMAP fields that widen.
NtUserFindExistingCursorIcon
NtUserSetCursorIconData

# The LARGE_STRING family. LARGE_STRING is 12 bytes on i386 and 16 on the host
# (PVOID Buffer at +8), so auto-thunking one hands win32k a wild 64-bit pointer
# that it dereferences under the USER lock — a whole-desktop wedge, not a clean
# fault. NtUserCreateWindowEx (above) was listed in M8; NtUserDefSetText was
# missed, and every stock window hits it via DefWindowProcW(WM_NCCREATE) setting
# the title from CREATESTRUCT.lpszName. These two are the entire family — if a
# new win32k syscall ever takes a PLARGE_STRING, it belongs here.
NtUserDefSetText

# M16 (task #43): NtUserMessageCall(FNID_DEFWINDOWPROC, WM_WINDOWPOSCHANG*) carries
# a WINDOWPOS by lParam. The guest passes a 28-byte 32-bit WINDOWPOS; 64-bit win32k
# reads it as 40 bytes -> field shift past the two leading handles -> garbage
# cx/cy/flags, so DefWindowProc's WINDOWPOSCHANGING size adjustment corrupts the
# window (collapses to 0x0, no WM_PAINT). The manual thunk marshals the lParam
# payload 32<->64 for this (FNID,Msg); every other message flat-passes as before.
NtUserMessageCall

# NtUserInitializeClientPfnArrays — INTERCEPT, not a marshaller. The guest's
# PFNCLIENT/PFNCLIENTWORKER are arrays of function pointers (4 bytes guest, 8
# host), and win32k copies them into the GLOBAL gpsi callback table, not per
# process — so a guest reaching that body is read at host width AND corrupts
# callbacks for native 64-bit processes. Harmless today only because win32k
# early-outs on ClientPfnInit and native user32 always initializes first; that
# is ordering, not a guarantee. wow64_manual.c returns SUCCESS without calling
# the kernel, which is exactly what the early-out already produced.
NtUserInitializeClientPfnArrays

# NtUserSendInput — E22, the size-as-an-ARGUMENT member of the cbSize class.
# marshalgen's WowAmSizeIn/Out rewrites a leading `cbSize` FIELD; SendInput
# states its element size in arg 2, which no struct diff can associate with
# arg 1, so this one is hand-written. INPUT is 28 bytes in the guest and 40 on
# the host (the union is 4-aligned vs 8-aligned, and each arm's dwExtraInfo
# widens), and win32k rejects `cbSize != sizeof(INPUT)` outright — so every
# SendInput from every 32-bit process silently did nothing.
NtUserSendInput

# NtUserThunkedMenuInfo — E22, and a trap worth stating: the PROTOTYPE says
# LPCMENUINFO but win32k casts it to PROSMENUINFO and reads `cbSize` bytes out
# of the caller, accepting anything in [sizeof(MENUINFO), sizeof(ROSMENUINFO)].
# So the payload is a CALLER-DECLARED VARIABLE SIZE, and a generated marshaller
# sized from the MENUINFO layout diff would have the kernel read past the end
# of its own 40-byte bounce buffer for any caller that declared more. Only the
# MENUINFO size class is marshalled here; anything larger goes to the kernel on
# the guest's own pointer, exactly as before, and the kernel decides.
NtUserThunkedMenuInfo

# Window/class procs crossing into the kernel (wow64_pfnmap.c). win32k keeps
# the 64-bit user32's apfnClientA/W as the system procs and picks an ANSI
# window's A proc by comparing against them. So a guest system proc must be
# swapped for the host's in the same slot going in, and a host proc coming back
# must be swapped for the guest's, or the guest calls a truncated 64-bit
# address. GWL_WNDPROC/GCL_WNDPROC go through the *Ptr entry points, since the
# 32-bit ones narrow the value and an unmapped high half cannot be recovered.
# Unlisted, the flat thunk returned the host's ButtonWndProcW narrowed to
# 0xb2057640, and user32:class executed it.
NtUserSetWindowLong
NtUserSetClassLong
NtUserGetCPD

# NtUserBuildPropList — PROPLISTITEM {ATOM; HANDLE} is 8 bytes in the guest and
# 16 on the host, and the size-only call reports bytes of HOST items. Flat, the
# guest's EnumProps* walked a 16-byte array at an 8-byte stride.
NtUserBuildPropList
tools/wow64gen/automarshal-win32k.txt:
# Syscalls exported flat-typed from win32u.spec (all 'long') that MUST NOT get
# a stage-1 flat thunk: their payloads diverge 32/64. Forcing them to stubs
# routes dispatch through Wow64ManualDispatch -> Wow64AutoMarshalDispatch,
# where marshalgen's GENERATED deep marshaller (or a loud UNIMPL) handles them.
# Unlike manual-win32k.txt, names here are still marshalgen codegen TARGETS.
NtUserChangeDisplaySettings   # PUNICODE_STRING arg (widening struct)
NtUserEnumDisplayMonitors     # OUT array of HMONITOR (count-aware; no codegen yet)

# E22 — the SELF-DESCRIBING SIZE family. Each of these takes a struct whose
# first field is its own sizeof, and win32k version-checks that field against
# the HOST sizeof: a 32-bit guest states the 32-bit size, the check fails, and
# the API silently returns FALSE/ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER for every 32-bit
# process. Widening alone does not fix them — the size field has to be
# rewritten too, which marshalgen now does (WowAmSizeIn/Out).
NtUserTrackMouseEvent         # TRACKMOUSEEVENT   16 -> 24 (no WM_MOUSELEAVE/HOVER)
NtUserGetCursorInfo           # CURSORINFO        20 -> 24
NtUserGetGUIThreadInfo        # GUITHREADINFO     48 -> 72
NtUserGetComboBoxInfo         # COMBOBOXINFO      52 -> 64
